candidates.name: Jinpukaku
candidates.reason: Closed for preservation/renovation work from Dec 29 2023 for approximately five years (exterior covered as of Sep 2025); only the Horyu-in garden and Hosen-an teahouse on the grounds remain open, so it does not survive as a standalone stop during this trip's window.

candidates.name: Kanikichi
candidates.reason: Tourist-oriented crab specialist in central Tottori city; also moot for this trip's Oct 20-23 window since matsuba-gani (the marquee Tottori crab) season does not open until Nov 6 — see disagreement d-crab-season.

candidates.name: Iwamoto Shokudo
candidates.reason: Well-regarded Kurayoshi yoshoku (Tottori wagyu x pork hamburger steak) spot that cleared discovery, but redundant with the wagyu pick already shipped for the trip's one Kurayoshi dinner slot; kept as a lead for a future/longer visit rather than shipped.

candidates.name: 20th Century Pear Museum
candidates.reason: Thin connection to the trip's two ranked priorities (culture/history, food); a nashi-pear museum stop trades time against the Sanbutsu-ji climb window and the party's limited-mobility pace budget for a low payoff.

candidates.name: Mount Daisen
candidates.reason: Roughly 90 minutes-2 hours outside the compact Tottori-Kurayoshi-Misasa loop the trip is built around; would consume a full day the 4-day, balanced-pace itinerary does not have.

candidates.name: Mitokusan Sanbutsuji Nageiredo Climb
candidates.reason: The Nageiredo climb is Tottori-chubu's single most famous attraction, on every English-language top-10 list — already Pass A's anchor pick (c-sanbutsu-ji-nageiredo-climb), so not re-shipped here by design (anti-default). This pass's contribution is the concrete access rules (minimum two climbers, footwear check, ¥1,200 total, 8:00-15:00 reception, closed for snow roughly Dec-Mar) folded into the shipped candidate's evidence.

candidates.name: Matsuba Gani Crab Dinner
candidates.reason: Out of season for the trip's Oct 20-23 2026 dates — Tottori's matsuba-gani (male snow crab) season is fixed by ministerial order to open Nov 6 and run through Mar 20; a generic guide recommending a 'matsuba-gani dinner' for an October Tottori trip would be factually wrong. Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) is the correct in-season alternative — see that candidate.

candidates.name: Kissa Sante
candidates.reason: Local-favorite framing and the all-you-can-eat natto-rice dish are single-sourced (na-na.media only) within this pass's budget — not independently corroborated, so kept as a lead rather than shipped.

candidates.name: Santo Mato Local Supermarket
candidates.reason: Genuinely local (non-tourist) shop per one 2025 local-media account, but single-sourced within budget — not independently corroborated, so kept as a lead rather than shipped.

candidates.name: Kurayoshi Shirakabe Dozo Townscape
candidates.reason: Kurayoshi's single obvious must-see, on every top-10 list — already Pass A's pick (c-kurayoshi-shirakabe-dozogun). No crowd-timing or off-default detail could be independently corroborated within budget to justify a novel Pass B addition beyond the food angle (Menya Hachibee) shipped separately; a single-source travelogue anecdote about declining tourist numbers was not pursued further since it would not change any recommendation.

evidence.claim: Hinomaru Bus's (72)(73) Misasa Line connects Kurayoshi Station and Misasa Onsen on the schedule effective April 1, 2025 (current as of this pass).

Weekday downbound (Kurayoshi toward Misasa) departures run roughly hourly through the morning, then thin to gaps of up to ~100 minutes in early afternoon (12:22 to 14:04), with the last weekday departure at 19:08.

Weekday upbound (Misasa toward Kurayoshi/Ikuta depot) service thins in the evening; the last recorded weekday departure from the Misasa-area stops (Misasa depot / Onsen South Exit) is around 18:03-18:04.

Misasa Onsen's own tourism portal describes the JR Kurayoshi Station to Misasa Onsen connection as approximately a 20-minute local bus ride, used for all listed rail routings (from Osaka, Tokyo, and Okayama alike).

The operator's own current fare table for this line exists only as a PDF; two fetch attempts returned unreadable binary content, so the exact current yen fare could not be confirmed from the primary source.

Limited express trains (Super Hakuto/Super Oki/Super Matsukaze) connect Tottori Station and Kurayoshi Station in about 30 minutes on the San'in Main Line; a local (non-express) train covers the same route in about 60 minutes.

JR West's own Tottori-Matsue area rail-pass page names Super Hakuto, Super Inaba, and Yakumo as limited express services covering this area, with non-reserved ordinary seats included on the relevant area pass — confirming these named services (rather than an invented one) are what a traveler will see on station boards.
The Tottori Sand Dunes themselves are free to enter with no admission fee; the dune-side visitor lots (e.g. the 180-car overlook lot) are free parking.
Sand Museum hours are 9:00-18:00 with last entry at 17:30; adult admission is ¥800.
The 17th exhibition period, themed Spain ("Sand World Travel: Spain"), runs April 24 2026 through January 3 2027 — so it will be on display during an Oct 20-23 2026 visit.
San'in Matsushima Yuran's standard sightseeing cruise runs March through November, departing hourly 9:30-15:30 (each cruise ~40 minutes); adult fare is ¥1,800.
The operator's own homepage confirms hourly 9:30-15:30 departures for the main cruise and tells visitors to confirm current conditions before visiting — cruises are weather-dependent and can cancel.

A separate general tourism spot page cites 'from ¥1,300' for boat options at this coast, lower than the ¥1,800 confirmed directly on the operator's own cruise-specific page — see disagreement d-cruise-fare.

The Shirakabe Dozo-gun district is reached from Kurayoshi Station by a city-route bus (~10-15 min) alighting at the Akagawara/Shirakabe-Dozogun stop, then a short walk; the district's tourist information center sits inside Akagawara Building No. 10, open 9:00-17:00.

Nageiredo climb admission is ¥1,200 adult (includes the ¥400 base temple fee); general temple admission without the climb is ¥400 adult. Reception is 8:00-15:00 with a 16:30 mandatory descent deadline. A minimum of two people is mandatory (no solo climbers); dedicated hiking-style footwear is required, and entry is prohibited in rain, snow, or other conditions the temple judges dangerous.

A free public viewing platform (Nageiredo Yohaijo) at the foot of Mitokusan was completed and dedicated in November 2022, roughly 600m from Nageiredo itself (partial view, obstructed by trees); it has designated accessible parking and lets visitors view the National Treasure hall without climbing and regardless of weather.

Jinpukaku entered long-term closure on Dec 29 2023 for approximately five years of preservation/restoration work; as of Sep 2025 the exterior is covered by construction sheeting. The Horyu-in garden and Hosen-an teahouse on the same grounds remain open, 9:00-17:00, closed Mondays.

Kabuyu public bath (Misasa Onsen's original source bath) is open 12:00-20:45 (last entry 20:15) in the late-spring/early-summer schedule listed, shifting to a 9:00 opening from June 2 onward per the same schedule; adult admission ¥400. An adjoining free footbath and drinking-spring station run daily except Mondays (footbath from 10:00 on Mondays).

Yakiniku Masashige Kurayoshi: dinner service 17:00-22:30 (L.O. 22:00) daily; lunch 11:30-14:30 weekends/holidays only. Closed weekday lunches, Dec 31, Jan 1. Private rooms seat 2-60 across the 116-seat restaurant. Four Tottori Wagyu course options at ¥2,800 / ¥3,800 / ¥5,500 / ¥6,600 per person.

The restaurant's own online reservation system tops out selectable party sizes below 8 and tells guests who can't select their real party size to call the shop directly — see disagreement d-masashige-party-size.
Matsuba-gani (male snow crab) season in Tottori/San'in opens Nov 6 2026 and runs through Mar 20 2027, fixed by national ministerial order — the season has not started during an Oct 20-23 2026 trip.

Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) season at Sakaiminato/Tottori runs Sept 1 through the following June 30, with fuller market availability from mid-to-late September onward — meaning it, not matsuba-gani, is the crab actually in season during an Oct 20-23 trip.

Menya Hachibee (麺屋八兵衛), a gyukotsu (beef-bone broth) ramen specialist in Kurayoshi (Fukuniwa-cho), founded 2009, signature ramen ¥780; local web coverage says it was once selected for the Michelin Guide. Hours and closed day could not be confirmed against a qualifying primary/operator source — see freshness flag.
US passport holders are visa-exempt for stays of 90 days or less for tourism under Japan's reciprocal exemption arrangement.

Japan MOFA's own visa-exemption page and the Japanese Consulate/Embassy pages returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt in this environment; japan.travel (JNTO, also an official Japanese-government tourism body) was used as the reachable official alternative for the entry-rules claim above.

Japan's emergency numbers are 110 (police) and 119 (fire/ambulance); the JNTO Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787, also reachable from overseas) runs 24/7 in English, Chinese, Korean, and Japanese and explicitly covers emergency support for illness and disasters, not just tourist information.

7-Eleven (Seven Bank) ATMs accept foreign Visa/Mastercard/Maestro/UnionPay/Amex 24 hours nationwide; Japan Post ATMs have the strongest rural coverage as a backup but run restricted hours (roughly 08:45-21:00 weekdays, shorter Saturdays, closed most Sundays). Convenience-store density drops in rural areas like the Kurayoshi/Misasa side of this trip.
Reference mid-market rate: 1 USD ≈ ¥159.4 (informational only — not the rate any card or exchange counter will actually give).

Climbing to Nageiredo requires reception at the temple office between 8:00 and 15:00 (last descent by 16:30), costs ¥1,200 total for one adult (¥400 main-hall admission + ¥800 climbing permit; ¥1,150/adult for groups of 20+), bars solo climbers (a minimum of two people is required), and requires non-metal-spike hiking shoes or rental waraji straw sandals (¥800) if footwear is judged unsuitable at the gate check. The route closes in bad weather and is typically closed for snow from December through March.

Without climbing, Nageiredo can only be seen from one place: the free roadside 'Haiden' viewing platform at the foot of Mitokusan — official wording: the only place besides climbing to see it — fitted with Nikon telescopes after a 2022 renovation, about 600m from the hall; the platform has 2 standard parking spaces plus 1 accessible parking space, with Mitokusan's own parking areas as overflow.

Dawn (around sunrise, roughly 5:30-6:00am) remains the quietest time to visit the Sand Dunes, but two independent 2025 firsthand accounts confirm it is no longer an undiscovered secret — other visitors are commonly there too by then, a shift both attribute to social media popularizing early starts.

Dawn (around sunrise, roughly 5:30-6:00am) remains the quietest time to visit the Sand Dunes, but two independent 2025 firsthand accounts confirm it is no longer an undiscovered secret — other visitors are commonly there too by then, a shift both attribute to social media popularizing early starts.

Beyond the main, crowded dune entrance, the official Tottori City tourism feature names a lesser-known 'camel commute' path (about 20 minutes each way) as an alternative approach route; around 9:15am the resort's tour camels can be seen walking this path to their work stations.

Matsuba-gani (male snow crab) season in Tottori is fixed nationally by ministerial order: it opens November 6, 2026 and runs through March 20, 2027. The official Tottori City tourism site states the season opens annually in early November with catch through March 20 and makes no mention of any October catch — October falls entirely outside the legal harvest season.

Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) landed at Sakaiminato runs September 1 through the end of June, with normal commercial market supply from mid-to-late September onward and peak quality November-February — meaning it IS in season and commercially available during an Oct 20-23, 2026 visit, unlike matsuba-gani.

Menya Hachibee is a small counter-and-table space with a tatami platform, and two independent 2025 firsthand accounts both describe it getting crowded at lunchtime — a walk-in plan for a party this size means arriving at opening or splitting across two visits.

Menya Hachibee is a small counter-and-table space with a tatami platform, and two independent 2025 firsthand accounts both describe it getting crowded at lunchtime — a walk-in plan for a party this size means arriving at opening or splitting across two visits.

A public route bus (the Kamii-Misasa/Misasa line, run by Hinomaru Jidosha and Nihon Kotsu) connects JR Kurayoshi Station to Misasa Onsen in about 20 minutes. A 2-day unlimited pass covering this and neighbouring onsen-town routes (Yu-Yu 2-Day Pass) costs ¥1,300. No train line reaches Misasa Onsen itself — Kurayoshi Station is the nearest rail head.

Some Misasa Onsen ryokans run a free reserved shuttle from Kurayoshi Station instead of the public bus — e.g. Misasakan lists pickup times of 14:10/15:30/16:20/17:30 from the station and return departures of 8:20/9:30/11:00 from the ryokan, by advance reservation only, with drive time about 15-20 minutes; each ryokan sets its own times and these can shift 5-10 minutes around train arrivals.

Hinomaru Hire's Kurayoshi office (0858-22-3155) offers 9-seat jumbo taxis — enough to fit a party of 8 plus hand luggage in one vehicle — as well as UD wheelchair-accessible taxis; jumbo taxis require advance reservation and are not available as a walk-up station-rank service. Standard meter rates in Tottori prefecture run ¥740 for the first 1.5km then ¥90 per 279m (regular cars) or ¥790/¥100 per 224m (large cars), per the Tottori Prefecture Hire-Taxi Association's published tariff.

JR Kurayoshi Station (rebuilt as an elevated station in 2011) has no-step access from both its north and south entrances through to the ticket gates, and elevators (no escalators) reach all three platforms from inside the gates; accessible toilets are available outside the ticket gates. The train-side transfer itself is fully step-free — the onward bus/shuttle/taxi choice outside the station is the actual constraint for this party, not the station transfer.

Kissa Sante, an old-fashioned coffee shop (喫茶) in Misasa Onsen, is described by one local-media account as a hidden favorite among residents, centered on an all-you-can-eat natto-rice dish nicknamed 'God's Table' (¥550) made with a premium local soybean; single-sourced within this pass, not independently corroborated.

Santo Mato, described as an ordinary neighborhood supermarket rather than a tourist shop near the Misasa town hall, is locally known for stocking 200+ varieties of dried fruits/vegetables with samples available to taste before buying; single-sourced within this pass, not independently corroborated.

reservations.releaseWindow: Online: same day up to 1 month ahead. For a party of 8, the online form's party-size selector tops out below 8 (confirmed by direct fetch of the booking page) — the site tells guests in that case to contact the restaurant directly.
reservations.actionDate: Call ahead once dinner-night plans firm up (this trip: aim for the Day 2 Kurayoshi transit day, before the last Misasa-bound bus).
reservations.partyRules: Private rooms run 2-60 people across 116 total seats, so 8 is comfortably within capacity — the constraint is the online tool's selector cap, not the restaurant's real capacity.
reservations.foreignFriction: Online form is Japanese-only; phone (0858-26-2919) is the reliable path for a party of 8 and lets staff confirm a room that seats the whole group together.
reservations.walkIn: Possible off-peak given 116 total seats, but not guaranteed for a party of 8 without a reservation.
reservations.alternatives: Iwamoto Shokudo (yoshoku, Tottori wagyu x pork) is a considered-but-not-shipped backup — see candidate c-iwamoto-shokudo.
reservations.fallback: If the phone line can't seat 8 together, split into two adjoining private rooms (2-6 each) rather than losing the venue.

reservations.releaseWindow: No advance reservation system — same-day registration only, at the temple.
reservations.actionDate: Arrive by mid-morning: reception is 8:00-15:00 with a mandatory 16:30 descent deadline, and the climb itself typically runs 90-120 minutes round trip before accounting for queueing at the chain sections.
reservations.partyRules: Minimum two people per climbing group (no solo climbers, strictly enforced); footwear is inspected at the reception desk — dedicated hiking-style soles required, rental straw sandals (waraji, ¥800) available as a substitute, sneakers may be turned away.
reservations.deposit: None — there is no advance booking to deposit against; the temple fee and climbing permit (¥1,200 total per adult) are paid same-day, in cash, at the reception desk.
reservations.cancellation: Entry is refused outright in rain, snow, or any condition the temple judges dangerous — this is a same-day go/no-go call, not a bookable slot.
reservations.foreignFriction: None to navigate in advance — there is no online or phone booking system (in Japanese or otherwise) to work around; the only in-person friction is the footwear/party-size check at the reception desk, which applies to every climber regardless of nationality.
reservations.walkIn: Walk-in only; no reservation exists to lose.
reservations.alternatives: The free Nageiredo Yohaijo viewing platform (candidate c-mitokusan-nageiredo-viewing-platform) is the honest alternative for anyone in the party who can't or shouldn't attempt the climb — see the sights write-up.
reservations.fallback: If weather closes the mountain, fall back to the viewing platform plus the ¥400 main-hall (Sanbutsu-ji hondo) visit, which doesn't require the climb.

reservations.foreignFriction: Booking runs through the ryokan directly (advance reservation required) rather than a public online system; a non-Japanese-speaking party should book via the ryokan's own reservation channel or have their accommodation booking site relay the pickup request rather than assuming a same-day arrangement is possible.
reservations.walkIn: Not walk-in — each ryokan sets and reserves its own fixed pickup/return times (e.g. Misasakan: pickups 14:10/15:30/16:20/17:30, returns 8:20/9:30/11:00); confirm directly with whichever ryokan the party books, since times shift with train arrivals.
reservations.alternatives: Public Kamii-Misasa route bus (~20 min) or a reserved 9-seat jumbo taxi.
reservations.fallback: If the chosen ryokan doesn't offer a shuttle or the reserved time is missed, fall back to the public bus or book a jumbo taxi.

reservations.partyRules: Seats 9 — covers the full 8-person party with headroom for hand luggage; bulkier suitcases may still need a second vehicle or a luggage-forwarding (takkyubin) arrangement.
reservations.walkIn: Jumbo taxis require advance reservation — not a hail-and-go rank option at the station.
reservations.alternatives: Ryokan reserved shuttle or the public route bus.

reservations.walkIn: Walk-in only — the shop does not accept phone reservations. A small counter-and-table space with a tatami platform, no private room; two independent 2025 firsthand accounts describe it getting crowded at lunchtime. A party of 8 should arrive right at opening or plan to split into two smaller groups.
reservations.alternatives: Other Kurayoshi gyukotsu-ramen shops appear in local roundups but were not independently verified this pass.
reservations.fallback: Split the party across two visits/times, or treat it as an optional stop for a subset of the group rather than the whole party of 8.

transport.route: Kurayoshi Station -> Misasa Onsen (Hinomaru Bus, Kamii-Misasa/Misasa Line, route 72/73; or a ryokan shuttle / jumbo taxi)
transport.doorToDoor: From the Kurayoshi Station bus stop, the ride to the Misasa Onsen area stops (Onsen South Exit / Misasa Onsen Tourism Center) runs about 20-26 minutes depending on the exact drop-off. Kurayoshi Station itself is fully step-free (elevators, no escalators, to all 3 platforms) — the last-mile choice outside the station is what needs planning, not the train transfer.
transport.transferReality: A standard route bus (fare box, no reserved seating, boarding by the rear door in the usual Japan local-bus pattern) rather than a coach — there is no dedicated luggage hold, so suitcases ride in the aisle/legroom area. Two lower-friction alternatives exist for this group: some Misasa ryokan (e.g. Misasakan) run a free reserved shuttle from the station on fixed pickup times (advance booking only), and Hinomaru Hire's Kurayoshi office runs 9-seat jumbo taxis (0858-22-3155, advance reservation required) that fit the whole party plus hand luggage in one vehicle.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: For 8 travelers including 2 with low walking tolerance and full luggage, this is materially different from a solo traveler's transfer: boarding the public bus with bags takes longer, the bus may not have 8 adjacent seats free, and standing with luggage on a winding rural road is a real fatigue cost for the low-mobility pair. The jumbo taxi or a pre-arranged ryokan shuttle avoids that risk entirely by moving the whole group in one reserved vehicle instead of relying on a walk-up bus.
transport.buffer: Weekday midday service has a gap of roughly 100 minutes (12:22-14:04) — missing a bus in that window is not a 10-minute inconvenience, it's an hour-plus wait with luggage and no seating guarantee at the stop. A 2-day unlimited local-bus pass (¥1,300) is available if the group expects multiple rides on this and neighboring Misasa-area routes.
transport.missedConnection: Missing the last practical evening bus (~19:08 downbound) leaves a reserved jumbo taxi or ryokan shuttle as the same-night options to Misasa; neither is a walk-up service, so they need to be arranged (by phone) before the group is stranded, not after.
transport.nextService: Outside the midday gap, the next departure is typically within 30-90 minutes on the schedule fetched for this pass.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Last confirmed weekday downbound (Kurayoshi -> Misasa) departure: 19:08. Build the Day 2 dinner in Kurayoshi to end with a real buffer before that, not against it.
transport.fallback: Reserve a Hinomaru Hire 9-seat jumbo taxi in advance (0858-22-3155, ¥740 flagfall + ¥90/279m metered) — one vehicle for the whole party instead of splitting across 2 regular taxis — or have the booked ryokan arrange its own free reserved shuttle from Kurayoshi Station. Nikko/Chuo Taxi (0858-22-7111) or Kurayoshi Kotsu (0858-22-1511) remain walk-up backups (~20 min), but the only fare figure located for them (~¥2,880) is undated-to-2009 and unconfirmed for 2026.

disagreements.topic: Uradome Coast sightseeing cruise adult fare: ¥1,300 vs ¥1,800
disagreements.investigation: The operator's own cruise-specific page (fetched directly) states ¥1,800 for the standard/large sightseeing cruise. A separate, more general tourism-spot page from the same booking-agent domain states 'from ¥1,300', which reads as either a stale figure or a reference to a different/shorter boat option on the same coast rather than the standard cruise.
disagreements.resolution: Ship ¥1,800 as the confirmed adult fare for the standard cruise (the figure from the product-specific official page), and note in the guide that a cheaper short-boat option may exist at the dock — doesn't change which cruise the guide recommends.

disagreements.topic: Yakiniku Masashige Kurayoshi private-room capacity: 'up to 6' vs 'up to 60'
disagreements.investigation: A third-party booking aggregator summary said private rooms seat 2-6. The restaurant's own site (masashige55.com, fetched directly) states private rooms run 2-60 across 116 total seats. The online reservation widget (toreta.in, fetched directly) confirms its own party-size selector doesn't reach 8 and tells guests to call the shop directly in that case.
disagreements.resolution: The restaurant can genuinely seat a party of 8, but the self-service online booking tool cannot secure it — for this trip's group of 8, book by phone, not the web form. This is exactly the party-size feasibility decision the trip's food pick needed.

disagreements.topic: Whether the Kurayoshi-Misasa public bus's exact frequency/last-departure time is confirmable from a primary source
disagreements.investigation: Pass B could not confirm the bus's exact frequency or last-departure time from a fetched primary source in its own search path (NAVITIME's timetable pages returned HTTP 403, and the operator's own PDF timetable would not extract as readable text) and, on that basis, treated the public bus as unconfirmed-schedule, favoring the ryokan shuttle or a reserved jumbo taxi for the return leg. Pass A, working the same operator, fetched hinomarubus.co.jp's own HTML timetable pages directly (not the PDF, not NAVITIME) and read the exact weekday schedule off them, including the ~100-minute midday gap and the 19:08 last downbound departure.
disagreements.resolution: Pass A's direct fetch of the operator's own HTML timetable is a genuinely read primary source and stands as the confirmed schedule (see ev-bus-downbound-schedule / ev-bus-upbound-last) — it does not change which mode is recommended as the anchor transfer. Pass B's alternative-mode findings (ryokan shuttle, jumbo taxi, station accessibility) are adopted separately, folded into the same transport finding as fallbacks that remove single-point-of-failure risk on the confirmed bus schedule for a mobility-constrained party of 8.

saturation.note: Merged saturation across both independent passes. Pass A: later searches on both ranked priorities (additional crab restaurants, additional onsen bathhouses, further day-trip peaks/temples) kept surfacing the same handful of names or options that were clearly weaker/out-of-scope for a compact 4-day, balanced-pace, no-rental-car trip. Pass B: final native-language search rounds (Kurayoshi shirakabe-dozo 'quiet backstreet' angle, exact NAVITIME/PDF bus timetables, a second corroboration for Kissa Sante/Santo Mato) returned generic tourism-board copy, blocked pages, or no new independently-fetchable specifics. Reconciliation: the two passes disagreed on only one point of substance (bus-schedule confirmability, d-bus-schedule-confirmability, minor impact, resolved in favor of Pass A's fetched schedule) and corroborated or extended each other everywhere else (crab season, Nageiredo climb rules, the anchor transfer's real friction). Two Pass B local-food leads (Kissa Sante, Santo Mato) remain single-sourced and are kept as leads, not shipped. Nothing unresolved across either pass would change which candidates ship.

nativeLanguage.why: Tottori-chubu's resident/local-blog layer — transit advisories, ramen-shop firsthand reviews, onsen-town local-food roundups, crab-season regulatory pages — writes almost exclusively in Japanese; English coverage of Misasa Onsen and Kurayoshi specifically is thin and generic (mostly reprints of the same 'top sights' list), so native-language search was the primary discovery channel, per src/data/destinations/japan.json's languages:['ja'] and t0Domains (go.jp/mlit.go.jp/japan.travel/jreast.co.jp families).

nativeLanguage.yield: Surfaced and officially verified an accessible alternative to the Nageiredo climb (the free viewing platform) plus the exact climb access rules (group-of-2 minimum, footwear check) relevant to the party's 2 low-mobility travelers; corroborated with 2 independent fresh firsthand sources that early-morning dune visits are no longer an undiscovered secret due to social media, nuancing the generic 'go at dawn' advice; found an official regulatory correction that matsuba-gani is out of season for the Oct 20-23 dates with beni-zuwaigani as the true in-season alternative; identified real Kurayoshi-Misasa transfer alternatives (ryokan-reserved free shuttle, 9-seat jumbo taxi) and a genuine party-size-feasibility food finding (Menya Hachibee's small walk-in-only gyukotsu ramen shop). Two local food leads (Kissa Sante, Santo Mato supermarket) were single-sourced within budget and kept shortlisted rather than pushed to a forced second source.
